In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Luttinger liquid is a non-Fermi liquid, and the Fermi liquid is a non-Luttinger liquid.
the anomalous scaling behavior is a general feature of one-dimensional systems with Coulomb interaction.
the anomalous scaling is due to the coupling of the chains and not due to a non-Fermi liquid behavior in the individual chains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that in one dimension the Fermi-liquid description is not a good one, but the Luttinger liquid is not a good description either.
the Fermi liquid is the most robust state of matter, and that the Luttinger liquid is a special case of it.
the inter-chain coupling is a necessary ingredient for the anomalous scaling, but not a sufficient one, and that a non-trivial scaling exponent $\gamma_{\bot} > 1$ is required.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anomalous scaling of the charge Greens-function in a Luttinger-liquid is a generic feature of a Fermi-liquid with a small inter-chain hopping $|t_{\bot}| \ll \epsilon_{F}$.
a Luttinger-liquid behavior can be realized in a Fermi-liquid regime, provided that the interaction is long ranged and the system is effectively low-dimensional.
anomalous scaling is a general feature of systems with long range interactions and it can be used to detect spin-charge separation.
